chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Jabir, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the meaning of Allah's saying: "And among men is he who takes for himself rivals besides Allah, loving them as they love Allah. And those who believe are stronger in love for Allah." And if those who were unjust had seen, when they see the chastisement, that the power is wholly Allah's and that Allah is severe in requiting (evil)."

He said: By Allah, they are the followers of so-and-so and so-and-so; they took them as imams instead of the Imam whom Allah appointed for people. And for this reason He said: "And among men is he who takes for himself rivals besides Allah, loving them as they love Allah. And those who believe are stronger in love for Allah." And if those who were unjust had seen, when they see the chastisement, that the power is wholly Allah's and that Allah is severe in requiting (evil)."

"When those who were followed shall renounce those who followed (them), and they see the chastisement and their ties are cut asunder. And those who followed shall say: Had there been for us a return, then we would renounce them as they have renounced us. Thus will Allah show them their deeds to be intense regret to them, and they shall not come forth from the fire."
Then Abu Ja'far said: They are, by Allah, O Jabir, the imams of injustice and their followers.
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'rivals' (andad) mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah verse 165 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the 'rivals' (andad) in Surah Al-Baqarah as specific unjust leaders who usurped the role of the divinely appointed Imam, establishing a hierarchy of devotion that rivals love for Allah. This interpretation highlights the Shia concept of *Imamah* as the central axis of faith, where political and spiritual deviation leads to the eventual separation of followers from their leaders on the Day of Judgment. The narration underscores that true believers maintain a superior love for Allah, distinguishing them from those who elevate created leaders to divine status.
